recipes.name: Happy Shrimp
ingredients_raw: 1 pound peeled and deveined medium shrimp
1 pinch cayenne pepper, or to taste

steps.text: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Stir in shrimp, green onions, and garlic; cook and stir until shrimp are pink on the outside and no longer translucent in the center, about 5 minutes. Transfer shrimp mixture to a plate and set aside.
Add tomatoes, cream, wine, basil, and cayenne pepper to the same skillet. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to medium-low and simmer until sauce coats the back of a spoon, about 10 minutes.
Add shrimp mixture to sauce in the skillet. Season with salt and pepper. Cook until heated through.

raw_recipe.headline: Happy Shrimp
raw_recipe.description: This spicy shrimp dish features a luscious sauce of tomatoes, cream, white wine, basil, and cayenne pepper. Serve with crusty bread or over hot pasta.

video.description: In this video, we'll show you how to make a shrimp dinner that's earned its happy title. Shrimp is cooked with plenty of garlic, green onions, white wine, cream, fresh tomatoes, and basil. Serve this up with some crusty bread or hot pasta and watch this dinner disappear.

review.reviewBody: Delicious and pretty as a picture! Just a wonderful blend of color and fresh flavors. Light, just right creamy sauce--not thick or too rich. I didn't measure precisely, just kind of eyeballed the ingredients trying to keep in proportion to the amount specified in the recipe. I didn't have cayenne, so substituted a couple shots of Tabasco sauce instead. Served over a bed of hot, buttered spaghettini (thin spaghetti) and "Baked Zucchini de Provence"(also from this site), this was a dish I'd be confident to serve to anyone. And it comes together easily with just a few fresh ingredients--cooking the pasta takes longer than it does to prepare the dish itself!

This is a great company and family friendly recipe. I can't have garlic, so I sub with shallots or sweet onions. When cooking shrimp, don't overcook. It gets rubbery really fast. It should form a "C" not an "O" when done. If they curl up and look like "O's", they are overcooked. This is also cooked with lobster meat or crab. Living on Puget Sound as I do, I use the Dungeness Crab. (Fresh, not canned.) I've made this recipe for about forty years. Delish!

Made this last night and it was WONDERFUL!! I used light cream instead of heavy cream and added bay scallops plus shrimp and it came out delious with a perfect light cream sauce. Served over angel hair pasta...SO Yummy..will be making this again!!

4 stars only because I think there should be a little more liquid (sauce) in this meal. If your making over angel hair pasta then it should be enough but I like to have a little more sauce with my pasta. Other than that this is a GREAT and QUICK meal to make. Even had a 5 and 7 year old happy!

I’ve made this three times now, but haven’t reviewed it until now. I’m giving it 5 stars because we’ve really enjoyed this in the past. But when I made it a few nights ago, it didn’t really WOW me. I’m not deducting any stars because I’ve learned that there are so many variables in cooking, a dish can often change from one time to another - different tomatoes, different wine, etc. I’ve made it with canned tomatoes and fresh and both are good. I doubled the sauce this time and served it over thin spaghetti. I know we’ve enjoyed this very much in the past, so I know I’ll be making it again!

This is wonderful. My husband only wants this recipe for shrimp. I double the sauce and add the shrimp after the sauce is made. Use whatever onion I have on hand. Cherry tomatoes. I find that 3 minutes is about all the shrimp need to cook. Add paprika, salt and pepper at the end. UPDATE: 1/14/24 I am now using half a lb shrimp, still doubling the sauce. Adding 1/3 cup grated Parmesan at the end, stirring until melted.

Delicious 10/28/2020
Increase cream to 2/3 C
Used 1- 14.5 oz can diced tomatoes
Add 2 T fresh oregano
Increase cayenne for a bit more heat
Add steamed broccoli back into sauce with shrimp.

WOW! I thought this recipe was too simple to expect much from it, boy was I wrong! My husband asked what this dish was called, I told him "happy shrimp" and he replied "is it because it makes me happy?" I added a chopped onion because I have onion with virtually every dish I make (sauteed with the garlic) and had two extra Roma tomatoes I needed to use up so I tossed them in too, I was also serving over spaghetti not angel hair so I mixed a tbsp of cornstarch (slurried in cold water) in with a 1/3 cup more cream and the thickness was perfect! I actually preferred the two extra tomatoes I feel just 2 would have been too little, they are absolutely divine in the sauce, the acidity cutting through that sweetness of the cream is toe curling! I subbed the white wine for white wine vinegar because I don't drink alcohol much and that worked just fine.

I made it Quarantine style...I didnt have fresh basil, so I used dried basil. I didnt have roma tomatoes, so I used canned, diced tomatoes (no salt added). I also didnt have heavy cream, so I used half and half. And to my surprise (and my husbands), It worked! T'was quite tasty!

I doubled the sauce, and used Cajun seasoning and better than bouillon ,chicken flavor, instead of salt pepper and cayenne The sauce is delectable. I could eat it as a soup. This would likely do well with another protein as well, like chicken

I tried to review this but only got halfway done, pressed return and voila it sent. So I wanted to make this quickly because I had the shrimp and needed to cook it. So I had to improvise. I didn’t have the tomatoes, so I used 1 T tomato paste (I realized later I had some sun dried tomatoes which would have been good). I don’t use wine in cooking. I was going to use chicken broth instead, but after sautéing the shrimp, I had a bunch of liquid from the shrimp. So no wine. I added 2 T of chopped fresh flat leaf parsley because I had it on hand. I also served this on white jasmine rice. It was amazing. My family loves it. It’s hard to find a recipe everyone loves. Yay!
I didnt have any cream so I just added some chicken stock . It was delicious. And less calories
So delicious, I added a fresh salad and my family loved it!
I've been making this for a decade, it's always delicious and it's so easy

I followed the recipes but did double the sauce as recommended by other's. No family member went back for seconds and that says a lot at out table. I tried it the next day at work it was better but I did discarded the rest after lunch. . I have had worse recipes so this gets a 3>

I followed several recs from others. I used cooked frozen shrimp so didn't add them until the sauce was already made. Even if I had used uncooked shrimp, I would have added them at the end. I sautéd the garlic and onions in butter and olive oil (1:1) for a bit, then added tomatoes, basil, red pepper flakes (instead of cayenne), salt, and pepper and sauted those for a bit. Then added sherry instead of wine and let it cook for a bit. I then added the evaporated milk because I didn't have cream and simmered it down to a good consistency. I boiled pasta and zucchini noodles and took about a half cup of pasta water and added it to the sauce and simmered a bit longer. Added the shrimp until heated and topped it over the noodles. Could make extra sauce or add some dressing to the noodles--though not necessary.
Absolutely delicious! No changes needed. The sauce is to die for. I've considered making it in bulk and trying to preserve it just to always have it at the ready.
made it and it was amazing
Doubled the sauce

I’ve been making this for a while but you definitely need to double the wine and cream. I also use a 14.5 oz can of diced tomatoes instead of cut of tomatoes. We do add more pasta though. With these additions I add more spices…oregano, dried basil and a jalopeno. My hubby often requests Happy Shrimp!
